finding: §8.2's audit paragraph defines a distinct audit next_action branch — a non-converged audit round with open non-PASS rows names the fix-and-re-audit directive ('address the findings, then tp audit <spec> --record <file>'). Test 14 pins review branches 1-4, audit converged (terminal marker), and audit clean-but-not-yet-converged, but never the audit fix-and-re-audit branch. That entire specified branch has no acceptance test, so its emitted next_action string is never asserted and two engineers would either skip it or invent contradictory expected values.
suggestion: Add to Test 14 an explicit clause: a non-converged audit round with open non-PASS rows names the exact fix-and-re-audit next_action, and quote that string verbatim in §8.2 (as review branch 2/4 are quoted) so the assertion is deterministic.

finding: §3.5 classifies a `--record <file>` whose file *content* still carries `fixed` rows as a usage error (exit 2). This contradicts the exit-code principle §3.3 establishes two paragraphs earlier: §3.3 ties exit 2 specifically to the case where 'the value is a command-line argument', and routes a fault that lives in *data/stored content* (invocation correct, fault in the value) to a validation error (exit 1) — 'the invocation itself is correct and the fault is the stored value'. The rows inside a findings file are data read from disk, not command-line arguments (only the path is); by §3.3's own criterion invalid file content should be exit 1 (validation), not exit 2 (usage). §6.2's `--harness-note` without `--record` is the genuine usage case (a wrong flag *combination*, i.e. an invocation fault) and is correctly exit 2 — which sharpens the mismatch with §3.5. Test 21 propagates the exit-2 classification, so the inconsistency ships into the acceptance suite.
suggestion: Reconcile §3.5 (and Test 21) with §3.3's invocation-vs-stored-value rule: either reclassify `--record` on a fixed-rows findings file as a validation error (exit 1), matching how §3.3 treats a data-resident fault; or, if exit 2 is intended, add a sentence to §3.3/§3.5 stating that an operator-supplied *input file* is treated as part of the invocation (usage domain) even though its content is read from disk, so the two sections agree on when file-content faults are usage vs validation.

finding: The verbatim next_action strings for branches 1, 2, and 4 are given, but branch 2 and branch 4 render the SAME action ('run the next review round') with different content: branch 2's string is pure prose ('revise the spec to address the blocking findings, then run the next review round') with no runnable command, while branch 4 embeds the concrete command ('run the next review round: tp review <spec> --record <file>'). §8.2's opening promises next_action 'is a runnable tp command where one exists' — and the re-review command does exist — so an implementer cannot tell whether branch 2's emitted string must append 'tp review <spec> --record <file>' (as branch 4 does) or stay prose-only. The exact byte string next_action returns for branch 2 is therefore unbuildable without inventing a convention.
suggestion: Pin branch 2's verbatim next_action string, and make the trailing 're-review' clause identical in form to branch 4 (e.g. append ': tp review <spec> --record <file>') so the same downstream action renders identically, or explicitly state that branch 2 is deliberately command-less because the intervening spec revision is the agent's own work.

finding: next_action is emitted on both --status and --record (§8.1), but branch 2's trigger 'convergence-blocking unresolved findings present' has no round scope stated. Branch 3 is explicitly cross-round ('a class that recurs across the recorded rounds'), and branches 1/4 key off the consecutive-clean-round count, so those are well-defined. Branch 2 is the outlier: on --status with N recorded rounds and §3.4's live recompute (an already-recorded round can still carry a surviving/unresolved blocking finding), the implementer must guess whether branch 2 fires only when the LATEST round has a surviving blocking finding, or whenever ANY recorded round does. The two readings emit different next_action values for the same state (e.g. latest round clean but round 1 has an unresolved critical), and the spec never pins which.
suggestion: State the round the branch-2 predicate evaluates over — e.g. 'branch 2 fires when the most-recently-recorded round has a surviving convergence-blocking finding' — and confirm that branches 1/3/4 evaluate the same anchor round (plus the cross-round consecutive count / class-recurrence signal) so next_action is deterministic on --status.

finding: Test 16 requires asserting that 'the prompt-generation path does not read review_converge_on'. This is a white-box internal claim with no direct observable — a QA engineer cannot write a pass/fail behavioral test for 'does not read'. The rest of the test (strings describe both settings, no contradiction) is observable, but the reader-set clause is not.
suggestion: Restate the untestable clause as an observable invariant: 'the generated prompt string is byte-identical when review_converge_on resolves to blocking vs all', which is a deterministic behavioral test of the same property.

finding: The newly added over-specification exclusion states that a recurring `over-specification` class 'does not trigger register-a-check and falls through to branch 4 (revise toward acceptance-level detail, then run the next round)'. That parenthetical is phrased like a next_action directive string, but it does not match the branch it names. Branch 4's defined next_action — and Test 14's assertion for the clean-but-not-yet-converged state — is the plain 'run the next review round: tp review <spec> --record <file>' command, with no 'revise toward acceptance-level detail' component. Since §8.2 is the section that fixes each state's exact next_action string (retained verbatim under --compact per §8.4), embedding a compound directive-shaped phrase (structurally identical to branch 2's 'revise... then run the next round') for a state that resolves to branch 4's plain command is ambiguous about what next_action actually emits for the recurring-over-specification, none-blocking case.
suggestion: Make the parenthetical explicitly non-normative so it cannot be read as the emitted string: e.g. 'falls through to branch 4, whose next_action is the plain next-round command — the agent's own remediation being to revise the over-specified detail toward acceptance-level altitude'. This keeps next_action emitting branch 4's literal 'run the next review round: tp review <spec> --record <file>' string (matching Test 14) rather than a compound revise-then-run directive.
